text:
Mara: heads-up — getting several support escalations about p95/p99 spikes for chat-generation across a couple of enterprise tenants since last deploy (around 1994999000). latency up 2-5x on long contexts. filing here so runtime / infra aware.
Kevin: ack - any correlation with the runtime deploys? which models/variants affected?
Mara: most reports on rwd-13b-8q (qat) and rwd-7b-flash (flash-attn enabled). Appears worse for requests with >1024 tokens and when there are many concurrent streams. Tickets: INC-4892, INC-4897. Customers include AcmePay and Shelf.ai.
Jason: looking at traces — saw a ton of KernelFallback events and some SDPA errors in the logs around 1994999500. repro on staging with load harness: p99 jumps when we cross batching threshold.
Olivia: can you paste the specific log lines?
Jason: sure — from staging node gpu-07: 
```
W runtime.kernel_selector: fallback to generic_sdp for op attention due to compile mismatch
E runtime.attention: SDPA kernel returned NANs for seq_len=1536, falling back
I kernels: selected flash_attention_v2 for model rwd-7b-flash
```
Mara: that NANs line aligns with customer traces. Could be quantization + SDPA interaction or a recent compile flag. We flipped -fno-fast-math to speed fp32 kernels last week in the linux-kernel-opts change (deploy 1994998800).
Kevin: hmm, -fno-fast-math -> we actually enabled some aggressive FP intrinsics. FlashAttention is sensitive to fp math ordering; SDPA fallback may be incurring heavy emulation path causing p99.
Anya: I'm running a reproduce script now with exact flags and quantization profile. Repro steps: 
1) checkout runtime@deploy/1994998800
2) build docker image with BUILD_FLAGS="-O3 -march=native -fno-fast-math"
3) start local harness with concurrent_clients=200, seq_dist=heavy_tail (50% >1024)
4) send model=rwd-7b-flash and rwd-13b-8q workloads
I can reproduce a p99 spike to 2.4s on seq>1024.
Kevin: thanks. Quick mitigation: can we toggle FlashAttention off per-model at runtime (policy) until we patch build? Olivia, any hotpatch route?
Olivia: there is a runtime flag MODEL_OVERRIDE.use_flash_attention=false that can be pushed via config gate. I can push to affected customers as an emergency gate. It requires a rolling restart of the serving pool though. Deploy-bot, can you prepare a rolling restart plan?
deploy-bot: scheduled rolling restart for pool=rwd-flash-pool, strategy=drain-then-restart, batch=2 nodes every 60s. ETA ~12m after approval.
Mara: let's do that for AcmePay and Shelf.ai first. Kevin, can you confirm this will reduce p99 and not cause correctness regressions?
Kevin: turning flash off will route to SDPA/generic kernels — weirdly that's what's failing for some seq lengths. But given the fallback thrashing we saw, disabling flash will force the compiler to pick the more stable generic attention path (slower per-op but overall lower tail due to fewer kernel fallbacks). I expect immediate p99 reduction.
Jason: small caveat: for rwd-13b-8q (8-bit quantized) flash-attention isn't strictly used — the issue there might be a new kernel selector bug that chooses an untested assembly path for seq>1024. I'm bisecting the selector change set.
Anya: while you bisect, we should also try a safer compile flag: revert the -fno-fast-math change (i.e., build with default fp contract semantics), and rebuild a candidate image with flash still enabled. If that fixes NANs, we'd know it's FP ordering.
Olivia: agree. I'll prepare a canary image with revert-1994998800 and run on a small canary pool (pool=rwd-canary-199500).
Kevin: also add temporary kernel selector override: KERNEL_SELECTOR.PREFER_AVX=0 and FORCE_KERNEL=generic_sdp for the canary — to test if generic_sdp is actually better.
Jason: bisect update: the selector regression appears introduced by commit 8a7c2f (heuristic to prefer flash when mem<8GB) — that heuristic mis-classified some seq shapes. If we patch to include seq_len check (only prefer flash if seq<1024) that might be lower-risk. I'll open PR.
Anya: repro results — disabling flash via MODEL_OVERRIDE reduced p99 on rwd-7b-flash from 2.4s -> 0.85s under same load. Reverting -fno-fast-math also removed the NANs for rwd-7b-flash in my local builds. rwd-13b-8q still shows tailiness until selector patch.
Mara: looks like two interacting issues: 1) aggressive compile flag (-fno-fast-math) causing numeric instability for flash-attn kernels; 2) kernel selector heuristic picking flash for long sequences leading to fallback storms and latency.
Olivia: action items: 
- Roll emergency gate: disable flash for impacted customers (AcmePay, Shelf.ai) — Olivia/Deploy-bot to execute (in progress).
- Build/release revert image without -fno-fast-math to canary pool — Olivia/Anya.
- PR to patch kernel selector heuristic to add seq_len upper bound — Jason (PR #2435).
- Longer-term: add integration test for seq_len>1024 + quantized models to CI and monitor kernel fallback rate in console.
Kevin: agree. add a runtime metric `kernel.fallback_rate` and an alert when >0.5% sustained for 5m.
Mara: customer comms — I'll draft message explaining we identified a runtime kernel regression, mitigation applied (flash toggled off), and ETA for full fix after selector patch + rebuild.
Jason: PR opened: #2435 — adds seq_len check and a safety whitelist. Requesting review from runtime leads.
Olivia: canary run results: revert image reduced error logs and p99 on canary by ~60% after 30m. No regressions seen on short sequences. I'm queuing a stable roll with the revert followed by selector patch deploy.
Mara: great. please post updated incident notes into INC-4892 and loop support on the exact remediation timeline.
Anya: follow-up repro notes I'll paste into the ticket: exact invocation, harness config, and the minimal binary build flags. Also adding a tiny test harness script to catch this in pre-merge CI.
Kevin: once we have selector patch + rebuild with safe FP semantics, we should consider re-enabling flash with staged rollout and perf monitors.
Mara: thanks everyone. After stable roll I'll schedule a quick postmortem next week to capture RCA and prevention. :thumbsup:
Olivia: done — flash disabled for AcmePay & Shelf.ai, rolling restarts completed at 1995001250. monitoring looks good.
Mara: closing the immediate customer escalation; keep channel updated if we see regressions.
